response.original_title: I Need You to Break Open My Heart: The Story of China's First Experimental Film Group
response.overview: From the Cultural Revolution to China today, the intertwined lives of Shi Jian, Wang Zijun, Chen Jue, and Kuang Yang illuminate a country repeatedly remaking itself. As Structure • Wave • Youth • Cinema, China’s first experimental film group, they helped shape China’s New Documentary Movement. Their films, including the eight-part Tiananmen, I Have Graduated, and Notes from Beijing, challenged documentary conventions, while programs such as Oriental Horizon and People’s Home transformed state television from within, bringing ordinary lives to the screen and putting cameras in ordinary people’s hands. Through interviews, film excerpts, and archival footage, I Need You to Break Open My Heart traces forty years of friendship, collaboration, and ambition. Yet their achievements coexist with unfinished films and unseen histories. An intimate collective portrait becomes a history of modern China, asking what a nation loses when it cannot confront, record, and learn from its own past.
